chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When the woman is in menstruation, prayer is not permissible for her, and upon her is that she performs ablution, an ablution of the prayer, at the time of every prayer. Then she sits in a clean place and remembers Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and glorifies Him, and praises Him, and extols His holiness, equal to the duration of her prayer. Then she is free for her needs.

key_terms.تُهَلِّلَهُ: She extols His holiness (tahlil/La ilaha illallah)
key_terms.وُضُوءَ الصَّلَاةِ: Ablution of the prayer (ritual washing for prayer)

ai.seo_question: What are the ritual duties of a menstruating woman during prayer times according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the specific ritual protocol for menstruating women, emphasizing that while they are exempt from the formal prayer (Salat), they must maintain a state of ritual purity through individual ablution (Wudu) for each of the five prayer times. The instruction to engage in Dhikr for the duration of a prayer serves as a spiritual substitute, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that the prohibition is on the specific act of Salah rather than general worship, thereby preserving the woman's connection to the divine schedule of the day.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the woman was in menstruation (Haydh), so the Salaat is not Permissible for her, and upon her is that she performs ablution, an ablution of the Salaat during the time of every Salaat. Then she would sit in a clean place and mention Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic, and Glorify Himazwj, and Praise Himazwj, and Extol Hisazwj Holiness like a measurement of her Salaat. Then she would be free for her needs’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Performing Salah (prayer) during a woman’s experiencing Hayd (menses) is not permissible. However, she should take Wudu’ as it is taken for Salah (prayer) at the time of each Salah (prayer), sit in clean place and speak of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, glorify Him, praise Him and say Tahlil, (no one deserves worship except Allah) for a period of time to perform Salah (prayer), and then go for her other needs.’”
